pr_body:
We await the predicate now.

For synchronous predicates nothing should change because the await will finish before the next protocol message arrives (thanks to `makeWaitForNextTask`).

Fixes #6199.

issue_context.title: [Question] How to wait for several responses that differs only with body?
comments: I think the issue here is that `waitForResponse` does not support an async predicate. So it treats the returned promise as truthy, and always returns the response that comes first, for both `waitForResponse` calls. We should fix that.

@dgozman What about https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#pagerouteurl-handler ? I have entirely forgot about it. It looks like URL can not be async too. Sorry for late comment, I am new to playwright.
@Kremliovskyi Yep, the route predicate cannot be async either. Not sure we can change that, but we'll consider - please file another issue for that 😄
@GetafixIT `async/await` should work as well, it was fixed in #6201.
@dgozman thanks - I'll try that 🙄 ... looked like it was an open ticket above

review_comments: why is it specific to sync ?

Because async predicate takes time, and we might concurrently call another one if the next event comes quickly enough. For example, responses are coming, and we are fetching the body to find the right response.
